title: Optimization landscapes of variational quantum algorithms
summary: Optimization plays a central role in variational quantum algorithms, where the objective function typically takes the form $F(\boldsymbolθ)= \sum_{m=1}^{M} f_m \left(\mathrm{Tr}[U(\boldsymbolθ)ρ_m U^\dagger(\boldsymbolθ) O_m]\right)$, with $U(\boldsymbolθ)$ being a parameterized quantum ansatz. Understanding the optimization landscape of such objective functions is crucial for assessing the trainability and performance of these algorithms.
